blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-accessibility-1 (Tab is captured inside the open sort menu) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: Do not intercept Tab (or Shift+Tab, which reaches this branch too since only event.key is tested): let it move focus out of the menu and close the menu, as the WAI-ARIA APG menu button pattern requires. Today a keyboard user who opens "Sort" and presses Tab or Shift+Tab only cycles through the four options forever; the only way out is to pick an option, which changes the sort. WCAG 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap and 2.4.3 Focus Order. A native <select> would avoid the whole custom key handling.
findings.title: Tab is captured inside the open sort menu

findings.recommendation: Handle Escape in onKeyDown: close the menu without calling onChange and return focus to the "Sort" button (button.current?.focus()). Today a keyboard or screen reader user who opens the menu by mistake and presses Escape stays in it; they cannot dismiss it without choosing an option. WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard; WAI-ARIA APG menu button pattern.
findings.title: Escape does not close the sort menu

findings.evidence: <button ref={button} type="button" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="false" onClick={() => setOpen(!open)}>
findings.recommendation: Bind it to the state: aria-expanded={open}. Today a screen reader user who activates "Sort" hears the button announced as collapsed while the menu is open, so the announced state contradicts what happened. WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value.
findings.title: aria-expanded is hard-coded to "false"
